title: playtest:grok-wave has no handoff, and the automatic promotion path has never fired for any vendor
body:
Found by the 2026-09-02 audit while answering an operator's question: "I ran 100- and
200-agent Grok waves — what became of the feedback?" The honest answer is that for the
Grok lane there is no automatic answer, and the repo currently cannot say so.

## The gap

`npm run playtest:grok-wave` (bin/playtest-grok-wave.ts, src/qa/grok_mcp_wave.ts) plays
the wave, writes session records and a manifest, and stops. Neither file contains a
single reference to `qa:triage`, `qa/tickets`, `intake/queue`, or `submit` — verified by
grep over both. Its own docstring is explicit that it is "not playtest-loop.sh".

`playtest-loop.sh` DOES run `qa:triage` after every wave (`PLAYTEST_TRIAGE` defaults to
1), which is the handoff most readers will find first. But that loop refuses any provider
that is not `runner_enforced` AND drivable, and Grok is operator-attested by design until
a capture reader lands — so a Grok wave can never take that path. The lane that runs is
precisely the lane with no handoff.

`loop.sh` can re-triage a shared corpus at cycle start, but only when
`AI_LOOP_TRIAGE_STORE` is set; unset, `triage_shared_store` returns immediately. Default
is unset.

Net: play a Grok wave and nothing reaches the dev loop unless a human runs `qa:triage`
against the store, from a checkout whose HEAD is still within STALE_AFTER_BUILDS of the
build that was played.

## Evidence this is the real-world path

Commit 69e368b ("File grok-4.6 wave playtest clusters into the intake queue", 2026-08-30)
filed eight corroborated defects from the 100-player grok-4.6 wave BY HAND, each with an
explicit `--key`. That is the handoff, and it is a person typing `npm run submit`.

Stronger, and the part worth acting on: `submissionFromTicket` stamps every
triage-promoted submission with the literal prefix "Promoted from playtest triage".
Searching every commit in this repository's history for that string inside
`intake/queue/` returns NOTHING. All 17 playtest-sourced queue items were hand-filed.

**The automatic promotion path has never produced a queue item in this repo's history.**
It is not merely unreached by Grok; it has never fired for any vendor. That makes the
three known gates (the unreachable `verified` rung f26bbd36141140f0, the reference-tier
shortcut 7250b22cf399b109, and the stale conjunct) less like independent nits and more
like one untested seam.

## Suggested fix

Two parts, and the first is cheap:

1. Give the Grok wave the same post-wave step `playtest-loop.sh` has — run `qa:triage`
   against `--store` when the wave completes, or refuse to exit silently without telling
   the operator the exact command to run. The wave already knows its store path and the
   build commit it pinned.
2. Cover the automatic promotion path with a test that asserts a corroborated, non-stale
   ticket actually lands in `intake/queue/` end to end. `tests/unit/qa_triage_cli.test.ts`
   already drives the real CLI over real directories, so this is an added case, not new
   machinery. Nothing today would notice if promotion broke entirely.

## Not claimed

The sessions are not lost — they are written to the store, and the tickets that triage
did produce are committed under `qa/tickets/`. This is a missing handoff and an untested
seam, not data loss. Whether the Grok lane SHOULD auto-triage given its operator-attested
evidence class is a product call for the owner; if the answer is no, the wave should say
so on exit rather than being silent.
